clue.text: Loner we led astray to become a worthless person

indicators.note: led astray means going the wrong way, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A solitary type is led into bad ways and becomes a good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led astray' looks like a phrase on its own, but 'led' is fodder and 'astray' alone signals the rearrangement of LONERWELED.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is an idle, useless character, someone who never does well.

clue.text: One's eyed anger

definitions.meaning: a sewing tool that has an eye for the thread
to vex someone, irritate or provoke them

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing needle has an eye, and to needle a person is to annoy them.

clue.text: Darkness descends with last bit of the puzzle

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word 'the' is taken

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: Gloom sets in as the solver reaches the end of the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue E 'descends with' REBUS, sitting on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erebus is the Greek personification of primeval darkness, and the shadowy region of the underworld.

clue.text: A lot will go down in value when this takes place

definitions.text: A lot will go down in value when this takes place

parts.words: A lot will go down in value when this takes place
parts.note: an auction lot whose asking price starts high and is lowered until someone bids

explanation.definitionFit: In a Dutch auction the price begins high and falls until a buyer accepts it.

clue.text: Child taken care of in hospital room

definitions.meaning: a minor placed under a guardian's protection
a room in a hospital with beds for patients

explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a child under guardianship and also a section of a hospital.

clue.text: Get examination paper for this assessment?

definitions.text: Get examination paper for this assessment?

parts.words: Get examination paper for this assessment?
parts.note: the paper is not an exam script but chemically treated indicator paper used to judge acidity

explanation.definitionFit: A litmus test uses litmus paper to show acid or alkali, and figuratively means a decisive trial.

clue.text: Poetry written by river — this one in Germany?

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Verse composed beside a riverbank, perhaps one in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written by' means placed beside, a charade link; the definition refers back to 'river'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river running through eastern Germany along the Polish border.

clue.text: Stop playing piano? Sad

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of the words that follow reorders them

explanation.surface: A gloomy musician asks whether to give up the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing piano' reads as music practice, but 'playing' rearranges PIANO and SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is one of the principal stops on an organ.

clue.text: Engineers with dirty accommodation were first to be given new arrangement

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a sty is a pig's filthy pen
led means were in front, came first

explanation.surface: Engineers in squalid quarters were the first to get rehoused.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyled means having had its style or layout redone, rearranged afresh.

clue.text: Participants in democracy get happy about 'Arry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: elate is an old adjective meaning joyful
to harry is to hector; the dropped H, as in a Cockney 'Arry, gives 'ector

explanation.surface: Voters cheer up about a Cockney chap called 'Arry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry looks like a name but is the verb harry with its H dropped, so the synonym hector loses its H too. 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters, those who take part in a democracy.

clue.text: Go by quietly with donkey

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for softly
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Moving softly past on a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to go by, as a car passes another.

clue.text: Item remained to be dealt with in the morning

indicators.note: like cards being dealt, the letters are shuffled out anew

explanation.surface: An outstanding item was left over to handle first thing tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante meridiem is Latin for before midday, the source of the abbreviation a.m.

clue.text: Girl endlessly stifling expression of horror jokes

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece wraps round the other
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
ugh is a cry of disgust or horror

explanation.surface: A girl suppressing a shriek at some jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LASS to LAS, which then holds UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughs are things done for fun, as in 'it was just for laughs', so jokes.

clue.text: A randy drunk following queen creates awkward situation

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the rearranged letters come after the first piece
drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A lecherous drunk trailing after royalty causes embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a dilemma, a tricky position with no easy way out.

clue.text: A time going over the area I have found to be fascinating

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means placed above what follows

parts.note: a tract is an expanse or area of land
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone finds the review of a period fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive means appealing, drawing interest, much like fascinating.

clue.text: Severely reduced, having suffered a deep wound?

definitions.meaning: cut back drastically to the bare minimum
literally slashed so deep the skeleton shows

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pared back to the minimum, and literally describes a gash reaching the skeleton.

clue.text: Observe the French saints without blemish

parts.note: to spot is to notice or observe
les is the French plural for the
S is the abbreviation for saint, here one of the saints

explanation.surface: Watching French holy men who live faultless lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean, unmarked by any stain or flaw.

clue.text: Dumping silly lass, do I weep finally?

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are jumbled in a foolish way
finally means only the final letter of the word weep is used

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether he will cry at the end after ditching a foolish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the act of getting rid of something, so dumping it.

clue.text: Spanish brute destroyed items in Dali's studio

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A Spanish thug wrecked things in the surrealist's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvador Dali was a Spanish painter, which ties the definition neatly to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintbrushes are a painter's tools, the kind found in an artist like Dali's studio.

clue.text: Monkey in old city — possibly a prominent feature

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
a chin is one facial feature that may jut out prominently

explanation.surface: A monkey in an ancient city, perhaps a striking sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey is a mischievous child, and an urchin is a scruffy, impish youngster.

clue.text: Have a wager on man, 26

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: to bet is to have a wager
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: Gamble on a fellow named Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 refers to the answer at 26-across, SELL, here in its sense of betray, sell out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out is to be treacherous to them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Excellent President not getting in the way of post-war charity

indicators.note: getting in the way means intruding into the middle, so these go inside

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian charity founded after the First World War, its name signaller's code for TH, Talbot House
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine president refuses to obstruct a veterans' charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Mistake admitted by holy English fellow in France?

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, holy
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A pious Englishman confesses an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre is a common French man's name, the French Peter, so a typical fellow in France.

clue.text: Journalist silver on top, not like a callow youth

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means placed above the other piece

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A silver-haired reporter is no inexperienced youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means old, the opposite of a raw, inexperienced young person.

clue.text: Composure to end when leader's walked away

indicators.note: the leader of the word has left, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: to cease is to end

explanation.surface: Calm returns once the boss has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means relaxed calm, poise, so composure.

clue.text: Bird shrieking horribly, loud coming in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one letter goes inside the rest
horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud

explanation.surface: A bird screeches dreadfully, its noise growing louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges SHRIEKING, and F goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a brightly coloured bird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Market coterie getting reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a cell is a small closed group, a coterie

explanation.surface: A trading clique gets into the news.
explanation.definitionFit: To market goods is to sell them.

clue.text: Tin, not plastic

definitions.meaning: tin is old British slang for money
paid in cash rather than by credit card

explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash in hand, available immediately, not credit.
